cards.observation_text: The lineage comparison places the animal outside the cat family.
cards.inference_text: Remove the feline candidate from the shortlist.
cards.bonus_fact_text: Pangolins form their own mammal order and are more closely related to carnivorans than to armadillos.
hints: The family tree passes near predators but leaves the cat branch behind.

hints.text: The lineage report places it in the big northern mammal branch: hoofed animals, cats, bats, and scaly anteaters.
This family tree does not run through the cattle and antelope group.

cards.observation_text: The forelimbs lack the elongated fingers and flight membrane of a wing.
cards.inference_text: The winged candidate is incompatible with this anatomy.
cards.bonus_fact_text: Overlapping keratin scales protect most of its body when it curls into a ball.
hints: The forelimbs meet the ground instead of stretching into airfoils.

hints.text: The body plan is not a horned, hoofed grazer.
Size estimate: small to medium, light enough for one person to lift.

cards.observation_text: The movement record excludes nomadic herding through Saharan desert.
cards.inference_text: The desert-herd candidate drops out; other social patterns remain possible.
cards.bonus_fact_text: It usually forages alone at night and can climb as well as dig.
hints: The tracks belong to one quiet traveler.

hints.text: Records nearly always show a single animal on its own.
Most of its activity happens after dark.

cards.observation_text: The diet record excludes specialization in hunting small invertebrates through loose coastal sand.
cards.inference_text: The sand-foraging specialist is a mismatch; other feeding strategies remain possible.
cards.bonus_fact_text: A long sticky tongue collects ants and termites from nests opened by strong claws.
hints: The feeding marks focus on organized insect nests.

hints.text: It is not a bulk feeder stripping whole branches of leaves.
It eats other animals, not plants.

cards.observation_text: The mapped range does not match the trunked giant's South and Southeast Asian distribution.
cards.inference_text: Cross off that regional range profile; this clue alone does not locate the animal.
cards.bonus_fact_text: Its range extends through parts of mainland and island Southeast Asia.
hints: The range tightens toward humid Southeast Asia.

hints.text: Climate reading: warm tropical conditions all year.
